Subject: Quick follow-up from today — procurement / payment path

Rafael / Marissa — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Great coverage on latency and the cost controls — we left with a clearer sense of fit. A couple of procurement questions from our side so we can scope internal approvals: 

- For an initial POC (30 days, low volume), do you accept credit card payments for the hosted API? We prefer that for speed.
- For production (manufacturer pricing), our AP team usually requires a Net30 PO and vendor onboarding. Is a PO good for Redwood? Any preferred billing contact / remit address?
- Does Redwood support marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace or similar) — Velox prefers using marketplace when available to simplify approvals.

Also: our procurement lead Samantha is on this thread; she asked for typical contract length, whether you require a signed MSA for Dedicated / Private deployments, and any SOC 2 / security docs we can review.

Can you send a short procurement checklist we can forward to AP? If you can outline the simplest path for POC -> Prod (card vs PO vs marketplace) that will help speed alignment.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Monroe
Head of Platform, VeloxAI
alex.monroe@velox.ai

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today — procurement / payment path

Alex / Samantha — great to meet you both. Quick summary and recommended paths so your AP/procurement team can pick the simplest option: 

1) Fastest (POC): Credit card on the hosted API — immediate access, billing on card, no SOW required. Good for low-volume experimentation.

2) Enterprise (production): Net30 PO accepted for hosted API and Dedicated. For Dedicated and Private deployments we typically require a signed MSA + an SOW (scoping compute and support). PO is used for invoicing against the MSA/SOW.

3) Marketplace: We’re actively listing on AWS Marketplace (coming Q1), but currently not all commercial SKUs are available there. If marketplace is required for procurement, we can accelerate the listing for this deal but it typically adds ~2–4 weeks to procurement timeline.

What we need from Velox for a PO route: 
- Official PO with billing remit details and PO#
- Vendor onboarding form (if you have one) — we can share our vendor info for them to fill in.

I’ve attached a short procurement checklist that calls out the most common AP asks (tax forms, remit address, contact, invoice cadence) and a link to our SOC 2 report. If you prefer, we can issue a preliminary quote/order form today to include on the PO.

Next steps proposed: 
- Samantha: if you can confirm preferred path (card POC vs PO for POC vs PO for Prod) we’ll prepare either a one-page quote (card) or a draft order form/SOW (PO).
- Marissa: I’ll loop you in to send the quote and pricing for the dedicated footprint we discussed.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call with Samantha and AP if that helps unblock.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Looping in a couple of AP/process notes from sales ops to make the PO path smoother if you choose that route: 

- Typical invoice cadence: monthly in arrears, invoice references PO# and our invoice number. We can accommodate quarterly if you prefer.
- Remit / vendor details we provide on request: Redwood, Inc. / 245 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105 / EIN: 94-3456789 (we’ll share formal W-9 if needed).
- Required onboarding items we commonly see: signed MSA (for Dedicated/Private), vendor setup form, W-9 (US), VAT registration (EU customers), and bank wiring instructions for ACH payments.
- If Velox requires invoice-to-PO line matching we can add PO# in invoice header and support minimal invoice attachments (order form).

If you want to keep the POC moving on card while AP completes vendor setup, we recommend: start POC on card, collect PO early and mark as retrospective billing for production. That prevents a long procurement roadblock.

I’ll prepare a sample order form and quick vendor data sheet (1 page) and drop in this thread by EOD Monday unless you prefer a call.

-Karthik

Thanks — this is helpful. Velox prefers to issue a Net30 PO for production. For the initial technical POC we can approve charging on a company card if Redwood is comfortable with that approach. Two requests from our AP team attached: 

- I’ve attached our AP policy and vendor onboarding checklist (Velox_AP_Policy.pdf). Please provide your W-9 and vendor address and we’ll start the vendor setup.
- We require invoices to include PO# on the invoice header and a vendor contact email for billing questions. Also let us know if Redwood can accept ACH or if you require wire.

If you can send a one-page order form or quote with total monthly estimate and billing remit details, I’ll route it to our AP for PO issuance. On marketplace: please share ETA for AWS Marketplace listing — if it becomes available before sign-off we will evaluate that path, but we can proceed with PO today.

Thanks again — copying Alex for visibility.
